tool_input.command:
git -C <repo> commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
test(doctor): guard four Unix-permission assumptions against Windows

Copilot flagged sandbox_removeall_test.go: TestRemoveSandbox chmods a
directory to 0o000 and asserts require.Error(os.RemoveAll(dir)) as its
fixture precondition. Both halves of the premise verified against
go1.26.5 syscall/syscall_windows.go before changing anything —
Chmod (:759) reads only S_IWRITE and toggles FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY, so
a read-only directory stays traversable and RemoveAll succeeds; Geteuid
(:1353) is `return -1`, so the `== 0` guard never fires there either.
New in this PR (7450dd2), so it is ours. Tagged //go:build unix, the
precedent procgroup_unix_test.go already sets on this branch; the file
holds only that one test.

Swept the class rather than the instance, and found three more in
doctor_test.go, all unguarded:

- "marker stat error is not read as disabled" — chmods a directory to
  0o000 expecting a child Stat to fail. Predates this branch (83e75ec).
- "unreadable hook file" — chmods a file to 0o000 expecting ReadFile to
  fail; a read-only Windows file is still readable. Predates this
  branch (4fb578c).
- TestCheckOrphanedAgentFiles_Classification's haveWounded fixture —
  gated on os.Geteuid() != 0 alone, so Windows's -1 ENABLED it, then
  asserted Perm() == 0o000 where Windows reports 0o444. This branch's
  own (0f8d015).

Each gets an explicit runtime.GOOS == "windows" skip, matching
archetype_check_test.go on this same branch. A whole-file build tag was
wrong here: it would have excluded the platform-split coverage added
earlier in this PR, which is the opposite of the intent.

Verification is compile-time selection, not runtime behavior — there is
nothing to falsify with a test. GOOS=windows go list no longer reports
sandbox_removeall_test.go and GOOS=linux still does; GOOS=windows go vet
./internal/doctor/ is clean; the affected tests still pass on this host.
EOF
)" -- internal/doctor/doctor_test.go internal/doctor/sandbox_removeall_test.go
